answer: Require each agent to post a refundable stake that is slashed when duplicate identities are proven, and tie reputation to sustained verifiable work rather than account count. Like nectar gathered flower by flower, trust should grow slowly through completed tasks and public attestations. An ocean of cheap identities then becomes costly, since every fake account needs its own stake, history, and upkeep. Reaching the summit of high-trust privileges should demand time, collateral, and a clean record, so mass identity creation offers no advantage over one honest reputation.
